def transform(grid):
    n=len(grid); vals=[row[0] for row in grid]
    known=[i for i,v in enumerate(vals) if v!=0]
    # smallest period consistent among known row colors
    p=next((p for p in range(1,n+1) if all(vals[i]==vals[j] for i in known for j in known if (i-j)%p==0)), n)
    seq={i%p: vals[i] for i in known}
    # any residues unseen inferred via nearest preceding known residue cyclically
    for r in range(p):
        if r not in seq:
            prev=max((i for i in known if i%p==r), default=None)
            seq[r]=vals[prev] if prev is not None else 0
    return [[seq[i%p]]*len(grid[0]) for i in range(n)]

import os
path='/home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-primeagentlearner-1792545456/attempts/2b17c2b4a8284089bbeaca60201f4326/system/state/workspace/programs/task-89b4e261.py'
# Must reproduce all demos; construct constant-row periodic + circulant diagonal completion.
source='''def transform(grid):
    n = len(grid)
    m = len(grid[0])
    # For horizontal bands, extend the smallest periodic sequence of row colors.
    if all(len(set(row)) == 1 for row in grid):
        vals = [row[0] for row in grid]
        known = [i for i, v in enumerate(vals) if v != 0]
        period = next((p for p in range(1, n + 1)
                       if all(vals[i] == vals[j] for i in known for j in known
                              if (i - j) % p == 0)), n)
        seq = {}
        for i in known:
            seq[i % period] = vals[i]
        for r in range(period):
            if r not in seq:
                # Fill a missing phase by the nearest known row in the repeating cycle.
                nearest = min(known, key=lambda i: min((i-r) % period, (r-i) % period))
                seq[r] = vals[nearest]
        return [[seq[i % period]] * m for i in range(n)]

    # Otherwise the grid is a diagonal periodic pattern: each row is a shift
    # of the same sequence. Recover the sequence from any observed cell.
    seq = [None] * m
    for r in range(n):
        for c in range(m):
            v = grid[r][c]
            if v:
                seq[(c-r) % m] = v
    # Demonstrations specify the full cycle; retain the observed pattern.
    return [[seq[(c-r) % m] or 0 for c in range(m)] for r in range(n)]
'''
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path),exist_ok=True)
open(path,'w').write(source)
